outcome: A Bash-tool sandbox that refuses to start says which of its six distinct failures happened and what the kernel told it: every PROCESS_START_FAILED raise site carries a named check in the established surface-detail idiom and a bounded, secret-free rendering of the underlying error, so one failing run names the mechanism instead of costing a diagnosis round to guess it - closing the observability half of sworn#251, where four CI occurrences across four different tests could not be told apart because six mechanisms share one bare code.

exclude: the root cause of the CI failures themselves (this slice makes the class diagnosable; the fix follows the evidence it produces, and a speculative retry or bound would mask the mechanism before it is named)
the bwrap argument construction, containment policy, and mask semantics (unchanged byte for byte; this slice adds detail to refusals, never widens what the sandbox admits)
the PROCESS_START_FAILED sites outside the Bash tool surface (internal/driver/invoke.go and aws_chain_linux.go raise the same code on unrelated paths and are not this slice's seam)
sworn#223, the CI provisioning step hanging before any test runs (adjacent and already tracked, a different mechanism at a different layer)

acceptance.text: Every Bash-tool sandbox start refusal names its site. The six raise sites that today emit a bare fail("PROCESS_START_FAILED") each carry a distinct named check, in the same idiom the native surface already uses for dispatch.process_signaled: newToolSession's invocation-scratch creation (internal/driver/tools.go:131) and its home/tmp surface creation (:137), and runToolBash's mask open of os.DevNull (internal/driver/tools_linux.go:505), status pipe creation (:544), bwrap exec start (:559), and process-group handshake read (:570). The sixth is materially distinct from the fifth and must not be folded into it: at :570 the sandbox process has already started and then failed to report its group, which is a different mechanism from failing to exec at all. The code string PROCESS_START_FAILED is unchanged at every site, so no caller, classifier, or existing test that matches on it moves. Pinned by a test that exercises each site's guard and asserts its distinct name.

The kernel's own reason survives, bounded and secret-free. Each of the six sites today discards the error it received - os.MkdirTemp, os.Mkdir, os.Open, os.Pipe, exec.Cmd.Start, and the process-group read all return an error whose errno is the fact a diagnosis needs, and every one is dropped on the floor. After this slice the refusal carries a bounded rendering of that error alongside the named check, passing the same validation the driver already applies to adapter-supplied bytes before they reach a durable record: length-bounded, and carrying no path, credential, or environment value that the existing redaction set covers. R5-S6 is what makes this safe to add - sanitizeFailedObservation no longer flattens a non-admitted diagnostic to adapter_failed with zeroed facts - so the detail reaches the operator instead of being scrubbed at the boundary it was added for. Pinned by a test that induces a start failure and finds both the named check and the bounded cause on the durable record.

The evidence is reachable without a rebuild. A sandbox start refusal is legible from the surfaces an operator already reads - the tool result the worker receives and the durable observation - so the next occurrence of the sworn#251 class on a hosted runner is diagnosable from the CI log and the journal alone, with no operator instrumentation binary of the kind contract-identity needed for its stream-cap hunt. Pinned by a test asserting the named check and bounded cause are present on the tool result surface a worker sees, not only in an internal error value.

constraints: Diagnosis only, never mitigation: this slice must not add a retry, a backoff, a concurrency bound, or a timeout change to any sandbox start path. The class is intermittent and load-dependent, and a mitigation landed before the mechanism is named would hide it - the same trap that let the contract-identity stream cap survive two wrong theories.

The refusal code PROCESS_START_FAILED is a contract surface: it stays byte-identical at all six sites, and the added detail is additive. No existing classifier branch, retry policy, or test that keys off the code may change behaviour as a result of this slice.

Every added byte is validated before it can reach a durable record. An error string from the kernel is adapter-adjacent input, not trusted text: it is bounded and passed through the existing redaction before it is stored, and dropped entirely if validation fails, never stored raw on the reasoning that errno strings look harmless.

The sandbox's containment posture is untouched. No bwrap argument, mount, mask, capability, or environment variable changes; a reader must be able to confirm from the diff that this slice only adds names and bounded causes to refusals already being raised.
